claims.text: Typical processing of HfNbTaTiZr yields a relatively homogeneous microstructure.
Elevated-temperature mechanical behavior in HfNbTaTiZr is governed by an interplay between lattice distortion and dislocation mobility.
Between 600°C and 1200°C, elevated temperature enhances lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Enhanced lattice distortion impedes dislocation mobility in HfNbTaTiZr.
Specific elemental interactions couple lattice distortion to suppression of dislocation mobility.
Suppressed dislocation mobility causes HfNbTaTiZr to have a lower thermal expansion coefficient than the baseline homogeneous state.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit slower elastic-modulus softening at elevated temperature than the baseline state.
Reduced dislocation activity stabilizes the elastic modulus at elevated temperature.
Reduced dislocation activity limits thermal expansion at elevated temperature.
The proposed lattice-distortion mechanism produces responses that deviate from predictions based on independent thermal effects.
The proposed mechanism applies from 600°C to 1200°C under elastic-to-low-plastic moderate strain.
Outside the specified temperature and strain limits, phase transitions or extensive plastic flow may dominate the response.
In situ diffraction, microscopy, and atomistic simulation can be used together to track lattice distortion and dislocation dynamics as functions of temperature.
The quantitative contributions of lattice distortion and dislocation mobility to the responses are uncertain.
